records.name: Trolley Car Table Tennis Club
records.summary: A table tennis club at One Falls Center in East Falls, open to players of all levels. It runs open play every day, a Tuesday league night and monthly tournaments, and it is affiliated with USA Table Tennis.
records.what_you_do: Come to open play, join the Tuesday league night, or take out a monthly or yearly membership.

schedule.text: Open play Monday to Friday, 6 to 10 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, noon to 5 pm. League nights are on Tuesdays at 7 pm.

cost.text: Daily play is $5 for adults and $3 for youth under 18, paid in cash. Monthly membership is $40 for adults and $20 for youth. Yearly membership is $360 for adults and $180 for youth, and a youth yearly membership is half price when a parent is a yearly member. League nights cost $5, plus a $5 club entry fee for non-members.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Route 32 bus, with a stop directly in front of Falls Center.

first_step.how: Walk in during open play, sign in when you arrive, and pay the daily fee in cash.
first_step.basis: The club says it welcomes players at every level and accepts walk-ins during open play. It does not list beginner lessons.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open play means you sign in when you arrive and play with whoever is there. The club welcomes players at every level, but it does not list a beginner session. Adults pay $5 for a day of play, and youth under 18 pay $3.
first_visit_tips: Enter Falls Center from Henry Avenue, turn left just before the coffee and pizza shop, go through the gate, and look for the club sign on your right.
Go down the stairs by the door nearest the club sign.
Bring cash, because daily fees are cash only.
Taking SEPTA? The Route 32 bus stops directly in front of Falls Center.

records.notes: Tier 1 said hours were not listed. The Play page now gives them, and the schedule and cost text are rewritten from it. The newest dated item is a news post from December 18, 2025 about winter classes at Mt. Airy Learning Tree, which the club posted, so status moves to active. Accessibility is not described on the site.

records.name: Twelve Gates Arts
records.summary: A gallery in Old City that shows contemporary art connected to South Asia and its diaspora. It holds exhibition openings, public talks, screenings and a residency for emerging artists.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery during open hours, or go to an opening, talk or screening listed on the site.

schedule.text: Gallery open Wednesday noon to 6 pm and Thursday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm. Tuesday visits are by appointment only, and the gallery is closed Sunday and Monday.

cost.text: Gallery admission is not stated on the site, and the page has a donation link. Some talks and showcases have tickets, and one student showcase is $40.

first_step.how: Visit the gallery at 106 North 2nd Street during posted hours, or get a ticket for a talk or screening from the all-events list.
first_step.basis: The gallery is open to the public on posted hours, and it gives a phone number and an email for questions. The site names no beginner programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visits during posted hours are open to the public, so you can look at the current exhibition. Openings, talks and screenings are listed by date on the events page, and some need a ticket. Tuesday visits need an appointment, so call or email first if that is the day you have.
first_visit_tips: Check the all-events page before you go, since some talks and screenings need a ticket.
The gallery is closed Sunday and Monday, and Tuesday visits need an appointment made by email or phone.
The site does not say whether a visit is free, so call (215) 253-8578 to ask first.
The gallery is at 106 North 2nd Street in Old City.

records.notes: Tier 1 marked admission as free, but no page says that, so cost is now unknown. Schedule text no longer lists dated events. Evening was dropped from times because the posted hours are daytime only. ZIP 19106 is from the contact page; the footer shows 19104. The accessibility page exists but gives no detail.

records.name: Unity Clinic
records.summary: A free primary care clinic for uninsured adults at 2130 South 21st Street in South Philadelphia. The Augustinian Defenders of the Rights of the Poor run it with help from Villanova's nursing school, and volunteer nurses, doctors and students staff it on Tuesday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a nurse, clinician, student or translator on a Tuesday evening shift.

schedule.text: Clinic sessions run Tuesdays, 5 to 8 pm. Faculty, nurse and student volunteer hours run Tuesdays, 4:30 to 8:30 pm.

cost.text: Care is free for uninsured adults who do not qualify for government programs. The volunteer pages mention no cost to volunteer.

access.notes: Interpretation is offered in Spanish and Bahasa Indonesian, per the Villanova page.

first_step.how: If you are a licensed nurse practitioner or physician, email phewson@augustinian.org, the volunteer contact the Villanova page lists for them, or use the ADROP volunteer form at rightsofthepoor.org/volunteer. Nursing and medical students go through their school programs.
first_step.basis: Clinicians need a license and at least a monthly commitment, and students join through their schools, so a first timer cannot simply walk in. The pages do not describe a first shift.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shifts run on Tuesday evenings. Nurses and nursing students take patient intake and vital signs and give immunizations, and they can watch clinicians at work. Nurse practitioners and physicians see patients and come at least one shift a month, and medical students work alongside a clinician. The clinic also uses translators.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own stethoscope, since the Villanova page says every volunteer needs one.
Arrive by 4:30 pm for volunteer hours; patient sessions start at 5.
Parking at the clinic is on site and free.
Nurses need a Pennsylvania license.

records.notes: Hours come from the current Villanova page and the ADROP page (appointments on Tuesday evenings). Neither page lists a clinic phone or email, so the phone and email are ADROP's general lines. An older search snippet named a different NP contact; not used, because the current page names others. A free clinic directory could not be reached (DNS lookup failed), so nothing from it is used. Status stays probably_active because the pages are undated.

records.name: The Arts League
records.summary: A contemporary art center in West Philadelphia, also listed as the University City Arts League. Artists teach adult classes and workshops, members can use open studio time, and kids can join an after school art program.
records.what_you_do: Take an artist led class or workshop, join as a member for open studio time, or sign a child up for after school art.

schedule.text: Adult classes run through the year. After school art for grades K to 5 runs on weekdays, 3 to 6 pm, during the school year, with snack and workshops from 4 to 6 pm.

cost.text: Adult class and membership prices are not shown on the main pages, so check the class page before you register. After school is billed as monthly plans for one to five days a week. Drop-in school holiday day camps are $125 per day.

first_step.how: Pick an adult class on the Take a Class page at theartsleague.org and sign up online, or use the Register link to enroll a child in after school art.
first_step.basis: Adult classes are open to the public with online sign up. The class list, times and prices were not visible on the pages checked, so a first timer needs to look at the class page before choosing.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult classes are artist led classes and workshops. Open studio time is a member benefit, so check membership before you plan to drop in. After school art serves grades K to 5 with snack and workshops, and pickup is from Penn Alexander or Henry C. Lea Elementary between 3 and 4 pm.
first_visit_tips: Check the class page for dates and prices before you sign up, since they are not on the main pages.
After school students from other schools must be dropped off by 4 pm.
Fill in the Student Information Form before the first after school day.
Use an email address you check often; the program contacts new families within a week of buying a plan.

records.notes: The adult class page (/adulteducation) returned HTTP 401 and /adult-education returned 404, so adult class types, times and prices are still unverified. The login wall was not worked around. A director email (director@theartsleague.org) is also published on the homepage. The Potter Pass, which gives ceramics studio access, is mentioned with no price or terms.

records.name: Uptown String Band
records.summary: A Mummers string band that practices in Langhorne, Bucks County, and marches in Philadelphia's New Year's Day parade. Its Tuesday rehearsals are at Uptown Hall, which it also manages as a rental venue, and it hosts public family events there.
records.what_you_do: Join as a performer, marshal or social member, march in the New Year's Day parade, or come to a public family event.

schedule.text: Music rehearsals at Uptown Hall on Tuesdays, 8 to 10 pm. Prop and scenery sessions on Sundays, 11 am to 2 pm, at an annex in Fairless Hill, Pennsylvania. The band marches in Philadelphia's New Year's Day parade each January 1.

cost.text: Dues and fees are not published on the site.

first_step.how: Walk in on a Tuesday night at Uptown Hall, or fill out the Join Us form on uptownstringband.com and wait for an officer to follow up.
first_step.basis: The site says Tuesday nights have an open-door policy and that anyone can fill out the Join Us form. Musicians take a music test and dancers meet the drill director to find their level, so the next step depends on the role.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tuesday nights use an open-door policy, and new people are placed by role. Musicians take a short music test with the music director, dancers meet the drill director to find their level, and marshals and aides go over their requirements with the chief marshal. The page gives no dues or costs.
first_visit_tips: Uptown Hall is in Langhorne, Bucks County, so plan the drive; it is not in Philadelphia.
Come between 8 and 10 pm on a Tuesday to see the music rehearsal.
If you play, bring your instrument for the music test. The band lists saxophone, banjo, accordion, upright bass and percussion.
If you do not play, ask the officer about dancer, marshal or social roles.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the band is based in Parkland. The Join Us page places its rehearsals and base in Langhorne, Bucks County, so the summary is corrected. Verdict is publish as a judgment call: the band is in the 2026 New Year's Day parade lineup (string band division), but it does not meet in Philadelphia. The owner may prefer out_of_area; please confirm. last_sign_of_life moves from 2026-10 to 2026-01 because the homepage event (Saturday, October 3) prints no year. The lineup page prints 2026, and the group's site gives January 1 as the parade date.

records.name: Urban Creators
records.summary: A North Philadelphia nonprofit working on food, art and learning. It runs Life Do Grow, an urban farm with a public park, an outdoor classroom and an arts space, and it has hosted programs there since 2011.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the farm or at a service day, schedule a group service project, or join the email list. Past community workshops covered medicinal herbs.

schedule.text: No volunteer days or events are posted right now. Volunteer days and group service projects are arranged through the volunteer page and by email.

locations.label: Life Do Grow farm and creative space

cost.text: Volunteering costs nothing. Donations are optional and tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer intake form linked from the Donate and Volunteer page. It asks about your experience, interests and availability, and the group replies with next steps.
first_step.basis: Volunteering starts with an intake form and a reply, and no volunteer days are listed right now, so the first shift depends on the group's answer.
first_step.what_to_expect: No volunteer days are listed right now, so the first step is the intake form and a reply. Past volunteer days were held on Thursdays and Saturdays at the farm on North 11th Street. The site does not say how long a shift lasts or what the work will be.
first_visit_tips: Dress for outdoor work on a farm.
Ask the group which volunteer day is next, since none is posted.
Group service projects can be booked by email.
The farm is at 2316 to 2350 North 11th Street, ZIP 19133.

records.name: Usiloquy Dance Designs
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance, and creates and performs its own productions. It offers classes at three levels and workshops for children, families and adults.
records.what_you_do: Take an ongoing beginner, intermediate or advanced Kalakshetra-style Bharatanatyam class, book a workshop, or attend a free public performance such as the Philadelphia Fall Arts Fest.

schedule.text: Ongoing Bharatanatyam classes at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. Class days and times are not published, so ask for the current schedule.

cost.text: Class fees are not published on the site. Ask when you get in touch.

first_step.how: Email shaily@usiloquydance.org or call 267-324-5917 to ask about the next beginner class. You can also book a workshop with the Book a Workshop button on the Repertoire and Workshops page.
first_step.basis: Beginner classes are offered, and the site gives an email, a phone number and a contact page to ask. Class times, fees and the studio address are not published, so you need to ask before you plan a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes use the Kalakshetra style and run at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. The site does not say how long a class lasts, what it costs, or whether a trial class is offered, so ask those questions first. Workshops are another way in: an introduction for children ages 7 to 12, a technique session for adults, and a family workshop for mixed ages.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the studio address and class times, since neither is published.
Ask whether a trial class is offered; the site does not say.
Watch the events page for free public performances, which the group lists by date.

records.notes: Class times, fees, studio address and trial policy are not published on any page checked, so the first step is to ask. The Fall Arts Fest date of September 19, 2026 comes from the Ensemble Arts Philly page, since the group's own page prints no year. Usiloquy appears only in that page's participant list, so its role there is unknown. The events page lists a Diwali event on November 1, 2026 at Burlington County Library in Westampton, NJ, outside Philadelphia; it is not used for Philadelphia status.
